takeaways: Use the LLM as the reasoning layer that understands requests and picks tools, while deterministic, self-written workflows and tools do the actual business work.
Production-grade agents need orchestration, state and memory management, evaluation loops, observability and clear decision boundaries, which Microsoft Foundry provides largely built in.
Specialised small language models and domain-specific agents will outperform general-purpose models in the enterprise on cost, latency and fit, but humans stay in the loop.
hook: Many enterprises put a large language model at the centre of every AI agent and wonder why it fails in production. This conversation with Microsoft AI MVP Karthikeyan VK is for architects and developers building enterprise agents. Learn why orchestration, memory, evaluation and deterministic engineering matter more than a bigger model.
